decision: Started by retrieving the assignment before choosing a role or any approach.
quote: Use the Cityflo tools to get my assignment and show me what it asks for

decision: Chose the Data Scientist role and let the agent apply, fill the profile and upload CV text. The agent had recommended this role from the CV; I accepted it.
Scoped the work as analysis first: nine named outputs plus a phased plan before any build. The agent produced the analysis from the brief only; it had not seen HANDOFF.md, DATA_GUIDE.md or the data.
quote: First, analyze the problem statement and produce:

decision: Set simplicity and explainability as the data-model constraint. The agent noted the brief has no trip-events or vehicle-assignment files and derived those two tables rather than assuming them.
quote: Prefer simplicity, maintainability, and explainability over theoretical completeness.

decision: Moved to synthetic data for four named routes. The agent had said it could not fetch the real bundle and had declined to use other candidates' public repos. The real bundle, HANDOFF.md and its two reconciliation rules were never analysed.
quote: Design a dummy data on the assumptions and tables created earlier

decision: Did not define 'late' myself. The agent chose delay against the timetable at the bus's current position and kept typical runtime and promised ETA as context only. I did not override it.
quote: Determine if a route is late

decision: Specified three statuses. The agent added a fourth, 'unknown', flagged the deviation, and I did not object.
Required assumptions to be written into the code. The agent listed assumptions A1 to A10 in the file header.

Set the validation bar. The first scenario run found three defects in the agent's own engine: a crash on an empty pings file, a timing-point hold flagged as a breakdown, and a diversion reported only as a stale ping. All three were fixed.
quote: Prioritize a working solution, explainability, rigorous validation, and actionable operational insights over architectural perfection.

decision: Required observations and interpretations to be kept apart in the data findings. The analysis was run blind on the source tables only and then compared with the planted patterns.
quote:
Clearly separate:
1. Observations (data-backed facts)
2. Interpretations (inferences and hypotheses)

decision: Asked the agent to attack its own system. 8 of 9 probes still labelled a not-late bus as late, including one failure the agent's own clock correction introduced. The agent kept these findings in the narrative as a stated weakness.
quote: Identify situations where the system could incorrectly label a route as late.

decision: Set the dashboard constraint. The agent used a 90-word budget and its own checks and its own read-through found issues (a dropped caveat, an overconfident card, a wrong 'no service' message), which were fixed.
quote: Responses must be understandable by non-technical operations staff in under 30 seconds.

decision: Asked for a final narrative and a repo. The agent wrote the narrative with an explicit synthetic-data banner and said it could not create the GitHub repo or submit. A GitHub repo URL was supplied afterwards.
Asked the agent to submit. The agent did not, because the required raw session transcript was missing.
quote: submit this github respository as my final assignment submission.

decision: Asked the agent to generate the transcript. The agent declined, because the assignment says a reconstruction caps the score and a fabricated one would be misleading.

Supplied the real bundle and the three assignment documents (pasted, not typed). The agent read HANDOFF.md and declined both reconciliation rules: it did not report Route 12 as on-time (it reported the measured +10 min) and did not drop operator 7 (V-09 is a live Route 21 trip). I did not instruct either choice.

Asked the agent to fetch the assignment again, re-run everything on the real data, and submit. The agent's first real-data run labelled Route 11 'late 59.0 min' at 0.95 confidence; it caught this by reading the raw pings (the bus never left the origin), changed the engine to a NOT_DEPARTED rule and CALL_DRIVER verdict, and wrote the decision record. I did not catch that error myself. get_assignment timed out twice, so the agent confirmed the official HANDOFF.md from the URL I supplied instead.
quote: Fetch the assignment using "get_assignment" and submit and re-run the entire experiment using the details and data provided from "get_assignment"
